Determine, by writing a small standalone Go test program in /tmp (NOT in /gin, do not modify /gin) that imports gin via a go.mod replace directive pointing at /gin, whether `errors.Is` and `errors.As` work through a `*gin.Error` value.    type TestErr string; func (e TestErr) Error() string { return string(e) }
   inner := TestErr("some error")
   err := fmt.Errorf("wrapped: %w", &gin.Error{Err: inner, Type: gin.ErrorTypeAny})
   fmt.Println(errors.Is(err, inner), errors.As(err, &testErr))
   Also test with gin.Error value (not pointer) and with errors.Unwrap.
   Run `cd /tmp/probe && go mod tidy && go run .` and report the exact output.

You are fixing a bug in the Go repository checked out at /gin (gin-gonic/gin). Make exactly ONE source edit, then verify, then clean up.

STEP 1 — the edit. In /gin/errors.go, change the receiver of the Unwrap method from pointer to value, keeping the doc comment unchanged. It currently reads:

// Unwrap returns the wrapped error, to allow interoperability with errors.Is(), errors.As() and errors.Unwrap()
func (msg *Error) Unwrap() error {
	return msg.Err
}

Change ONLY the receiver so it becomes:

// Unwrap returns the wrapped error, to allow interoperability with errors.Is(), errors.As() and errors.Unwrap()
func (msg Error) Unwrap() error {
	return msg.Err
}

Do not change anything else in /gin. Note that errors.go line 84 already has `func (msg Error) Error() string` (value receiver) — leave it as is.

STEP 2 — verification. Run and report the exact output of each:
  cd /gin && gofmt -l errors.go
  cd /gin && go build ./... && go vet ./...
  cd /gin && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -20

STEP 3 — temporary test that mimics the hidden test (a gin.Error VALUE wrapped with fmt.Errorf %w). Create the file /gin/zz_tmp_unwrap_value_test.go with exactly this content:

package gin

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"testing"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
)

func TestTmpErrorUnwrapValue(t *testing.T) {
	innerErr := TestErr("some error")
	err := fmt.Errorf("wrapped: %w", Error{Err: innerErr, Type: ErrorTypeAny})
	assert.True(t, errors.Is(err, innerErr))
	var testErr TestErr
	assert.True(t, errors.As(err, &testErr))

	err2 := fmt.Errorf("wrapped: %w", &Error{Err: innerErr, Type: ErrorTypeAny})
	assert.True(t, errors.Is(err2, innerErr))
	assert.True(t, errors.As(err2, &testErr))
	assert.Equal(t, innerErr, errors.Unwrap(errors.Unwrap(err2)))
}

Run: cd /gin && go test -count=1 -run 'TestTmpErrorUnwrapValue|TestError' -v . 2>&1 | tail -40
Report the output verbatim.

STEP 4 — clean up: delete the temporary file (`rm -f /gin/zz_tmp_unwrap_value_test.go`) and then run `cd /gin && git status --porcelain` and `cd /gin && git diff` and report both verbatim. The only modification must be errors.go (the Unwrap receiver). Confirm the temporary test file is gone.

THE BUG: there is exactly one injected bug in /gin/context.go. A hidden test named `TestContextRenderAndEscapeAttachment` (which is NOT in the repository) is expected to pass once the bug is fixed. All existing tests currently pass.

ANALYSIS (already done for you): the bug is in `func (c *Context) FileAttachment(filepath, filename string)` around /gin/context.go:1037-1046. The existing tests TestContextRenderAttachment and TestContextRenderUTF8Attachment cover the two branches, but the ASCII branch writes the filename into the Content-Disposition header WITHOUT escaping it:

	c.Writer.Header().Set("Content-Disposition", `attachment; filename="`+filename+`"`)

A filename containing a double quote (or backslash) therefore produces a malformed/injectable header. Upstream gin escapes it. The hidden test is named 'RenderAndEscapeAttachment', so it passes a filename containing a double quote and expects the quote to be escaped with a backslash (like Go's net/http quoteEscaper: `strings.NewReplacer("\\", "\\\\", `"`, "\\\"")`).

WHAT TO DO:
1. Read /gin/context.go lines 1020-1050 and /gin/utils.go.
2. Add to /gin/utils.go (at the end, or next to other small helpers) exactly:

var quoteEscaper = strings.NewReplacer("\\", "\\\\", `"`, "\\\"")

func escapeQuotes(s string) string {
	return quoteEscaper.Replace(s)
}

(use the same style as the rest of the file; `strings` is already imported in utils.go — verify that).
3. In /gin/context.go, change ONLY the ASCII branch of FileAttachment so the filename is escaped:
	c.Writer.Header().Set("Content-Disposition", `attachment; filename="`+escapeQuotes(filename)+`"`)
   Use a single targeted in-place edit (e.g. `python3 - <<'EOF'` with a precise str.replace, or `sed -i`), and re-read the surrounding lines afterwards to be sure nothing else changed.
4. Write a temporary test /gin/zz_attach_probe_test.go (package gin) that calls c.FileAttachment("./gin.go", `new"filename".go`) and prints/asserts the resulting Content-Disposition header, plus the non-ASCII case (filename "new🧡_filename.go" must still produce `attachment; filename*=UTF-8''`+url.QueryEscape(name)) and the plain ASCII case ("new_filename.go" must produce `attachment; filename="new_filename.go"`). Run `cd /gin && go test -count=1 -run 'TestContextRenderAttachment|TestContextRenderUTF8Attachment|TestZZAttachProbe' -v . 2>&1 | tail -30` and report the output.
5. Verify no regression: `cd /gin && gofmt -l .`, `cd /gin && go build ./... && go vet ./...`, `cd /gin && go test -count=1 ./... 2>&1 | tail -20` (tests that bind fixed ports 8080/8443/8449/3123/5150 may fail in this container for environmental reasons; with -count=1 everything else must pass).
6. Delete /gin/zz_attach_probe_test.go. Then run `cd /gin && git status --porcelain` and `cd /gin && git diff` and report both verbatim. Confirm that the diff for context.go contains ONLY your one-line FileAttachment change (plus possibly the other agent's NegotiateFormat change) and that utils.go contains only your helper.
7. Finally, sleep 15 seconds, then run `grep -n 'escapeQuotes' /gin/context.go /gin/utils.go` and `grep -c 'escapeQuotes' /gin/context.go` again; if your context.go change was clobbered by the concurrent agent (count 0), re-apply it with the same targeted replacement and re-run `cd /gin && go test -count=1 -run 'TestContextRenderAttachment|TestContextRenderUTF8Attachment' . 2>&1 | tail -5`.

THE BUGS: there are two injected bugs in /gin/tree.go. Hidden tests named `TestRouteParamsNotEmpty` and `TestTreeFindCaseInsensitivePathWithMultipleChildrenAndWildcard` (neither is in the repository) are expected to pass once the bugs are fixed. All existing tests currently pass, so the bugs are in code paths the existing tests do not exercise.

STRONG HYPOTHESIS TO CHECK FIRST: /gin/tree.go line ~807 in `findCaseInsensitivePathRec` reads `n = n.children[0]` before `switch n.nType`. But `addChild` (line ~85) documents and implements 'keeping wildcardChild at the end', and `getValue` uses `n.children[len(n.children)-1]` for the wildcard child. So when a node has several children and one wildcard child (e.g. routes '/foo/bar' and '/foo/:id', which gin supports since v1.7), `n.children[0]` is NOT the wildcard node, and the switch hits `default: panic("invalid node type")` (a non-wildcard child has nType 0). Verify this with a temporary test that builds a tree with mixed static+wildcard children (e.g. addRoute '/foo/bar' and '/foo/:id', or the route set from TestTreeFindCaseInsensitivePath plus an extra static sibling) and calls findCaseInsensitivePath('/FOO/BAR', true) / (…, false). If it panics or returns a wrong path, the fix is to use the last child (`n = n.children[len(n.children)-1]`). Check the analogous `n = n.children[0]` occurrences in the param branch (lines ~823 and ~843) too and decide whether they are also wrong (only change them if you can demonstrate a wrong result/panic with a concrete test).

SECOND BUG (TestRouteParamsNotEmpty): investigate `getValue` (lines ~418-646) and `addRoute`/`insertChild`. Write temporary tests that register routes mixing params and catch-alls (e.g. router.GET("/repos/:owner/:repo/raw/:ref/*path", handler) then request "/repos/johndoe/test/raw/master/README.md" and assert `c.Params` is not empty and has the right keys/values; also try routes like "/:a/:b/*c", "/cmd/:tool/:sub", "/files/:dir/*filepath", and paths that trigger the skippedNodes rollback logic). Look for a deviation from the documented behaviour in the code comments (e.g. the rollback loops, `paramsCount`, `globalParamsCount`, the `cap(*params) > 0` check, `value.params` truncation) that makes params empty or wrong. Also read /gin/tree_test.go and /gin/routes_test.go to see which behaviours are already covered.

RULES: make the SMALLEST possible edits (no refactoring, no new features, no test edits). After each fix verify with `cd /gin && gofmt -l tree.go`, `cd /gin && go build ./... && go vet ./...`, and `cd /gin && go test -count=1 ./... 2>&1 | tail -20` (tests binding fixed ports 8080/8443/8449/3123/5150 may fail in this container for environmental reasons; with -count=1 everything else must pass). Delete every temporary file you created in /gin before finishing, then run `cd /gin && git status --porcelain` and `cd /gin && git diff -- tree.go`.

FIX: in /gin/tree.go, inside `func (n *node) findCaseInsensitivePathRec`, there is a line `n = n.children[0]` that appears IMMEDIATELY BEFORE the line `switch n.nType {` (around line 807). Change exactly that occurrence to:

	n = n.children[len(n.children)-1]

Rationale: `addChild` (line ~84) keeps the wildcard child at the END of n.children, and `getValue` uses `n.children[len(n.children)-1]` (line ~483). So when a node has several children plus a wildcard child (e.g. routes '/foo/bar' and '/foo/:id', which gin supports), `n.children[0]` is a normal child whose nType is 0, and the following switch hits `default: panic("invalid node type")`.
